name: Dlib (dnn module, CUDA/cuDNN deep learning API)
workload: Deep neural network speed on GPU compared with Caffe; the search-result text gives no network, batch size, or whether it is training or inference.
claimed_speedup: Fast mode about 1.6x faster than Caffe at about 1.5x the VRAM; low-VRAM mode about 0.85x Caffe's speed at about half the memory (author's blog, June 2016; snippet only)
tradeoffs: Fast mode trades about 1.5x more VRAM for speed; a low-VRAM mode halves memory at about 0.85x of Caffe's speed. Dlib is a broad toolkit (ML, imaging, optimization, networking) and the dnn module is one component of it.
caveats: Snippet only: blog.dlib.net could not be fetched (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND), so the numbers come from WebSearch result text for the June 2016 blog archive page and the exact post, network, GPU, cuDNN version, batch size and flags are unverified. First-party author claim from 2016 against 2016-era Caffe and cuDNN; both have changed greatly since. Dlib's own docs and release notes (docs/docs/release_notes.xml) contain only dlib-versus-dlib speedups (CNN+MMOD detectors 2.5x faster, 98 fps versus 39 fps) and no other external baseline. Third-party reports in dlib GitHub discussions (video reading against OpenCV cv::VideoCapture) are mixed and trace mostly to thread-count defaults, so they do not support a speed win. The awesome-cpp baselines guess (system I/O or threading) was wrong for this project.
